definitions.explanation: A building method in which the structural frame is made of steel. A standard category in Japanese real-estate listings, often abbreviated S{造|ぞう}.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}だ。
{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦アパート→アパート：01012_apaato⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}している→探す：00493_sagasu⟧。
examples.english: I'm looking for a steel-framed apartment.

examples.japanese: ⟦{木造|もくぞう}→木造：08328_mokuzou⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ほう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{防音性|ぼうおんせい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Steel-frame construction is said to have better soundproofing than wooden construction.

notes:
Formed from ⟦{鉄骨|てっこつ}→鉄骨：24552_tekkotsu⟧ (steel frame) + {造|ぞう} (construction, build). One of the main structural categories listed when renting or buying property in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧: a steel-frame apartment building
- ⟦{軽量|けいりょう}→軽量：19124_keiryou⟧{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}: light-gauge steel construction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{木造|もくぞう}→木造：08328_mokuzou⟧: wooden construction — frame built of wood; generally cheaper but less soundproof
- ⟦{鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート→鉄筋コンクリート：17904_tekkinkonkuriito⟧{造|ぞう}: reinforced-concrete construction — uses steel-reinforced concrete; more durable and soundproof than steel-frame alone
